classification.difficultyReason: Links symbolic intercepts to the midpoint formula, then uses explicitly requested substitution and triangle area to establish two results; the parts supply the route without an unsignposted insight.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The line $y=-\frac14b^2x+b$, where $b\ne0$, has intercepts at $A$ and $B$. Find the coordinates of $P$, the midpoint of $AB$.

answer.worked:
At the $y$-intercept, $x=0$, so $y=b$. At the $x$-intercept:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-\frac14b^2x+b\\\frac14b^2x&=b\\x&=\frac4b.\end{align*}$$
Thus the intercepts are $\left(\frac4b,0\right)$ and $(0,b)$. Taking the mean of each pair of coordinates,
$$P=\left(\frac{\frac4b+0}{2},\frac{0+b}{2}\right)=\left(\frac2b,\frac b2\right).$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $P$ lies on the hyperbola $y=\frac1x$.

answer.short: At $P$, $\frac1x=\frac{1}{\frac{2}{b}}=\frac b2=y$, so $P$ lies on the hyperbola.
answer.worked:
Substitute the $x$-coordinate of $P$ into the hyperbola:
$$\begin{align*}\frac1x&=\frac{1}{2/b}\\\frac1x&=\frac b2.\end{align*}$$
This equals the $y$-coordinate of $P$, so $P$ lies on $y=\frac1x$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the area of $\triangle OAB$, where $O$ is the origin, is independent of the value of $b$.

answer.short:
$2\text{ units}^2$, independent of $b$.

Use half the product of the perpendicular intercept lengths.
answer.worked:
The perpendicular sides along the axes have lengths $\left|\frac4b\right|$ and $|b|$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=\frac12\left|\frac4b\right||b|\\\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=\frac12\left|\frac4b\times b\right|\\\text{Area of }\triangle OAB&=2\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
The area is constant and therefore independent of $b$.
